requirement:
`habeas test` MUST run the full-workspace instrumented nextest workflow of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.run` and, only after that workflow succeeds,
run the post-suite check of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check`. It MUST
return a failing exit status if test execution, coverage collection, or the
post-suite check fails. It MUST NOT author exception evidence or invoke an
assessment model.
rationale:
The three marked tests in `tests/execution_coverage.rs` cover each obligation of `requirements.test-coverage.test`. All of them run the real `habeas test` binary through the `full_flow` helper.

- **Full-workspace instrumented nextest run, then the check.**
  - `fn[full_test_flow_checks_real_function_counters_after_all_tests]` runs a fixture with sync, async and integration tests.
  - It asserts success and "Coverage check passed" in stdout.
  - It asserts that the saved run has four attempts, so unit and integration targets were all executed. Every attempt has non-empty per-process function data.
  - It asserts that `coverage-check` on the saved result also passes.
- **Failure when the post-suite check fails.**
  - The same test then rewrites the source so that `fn[hidden]` is never executed.
  - It asserts a non-zero exit status.
  - It asserts that stdout names the zero-execution function.
  - It asserts that the saved run's outcome is still "success", so the test suite passed and the failure came from the check.
- **Failure when test execution fails, and no check afterwards.** `fn[failed_suite_stops_full_flow_before_the_coverage_check]` uses a panicking test. It asserts a failing exit status and that stdout has no "Coverage check" text, so the check did not run. It asserts that the run outcome is "failed".
- **Failure when coverage collection fails, and no check afterwards.**
  - `fn[passing_tests_with_missing_or_corrupt_profiles_fail_collection_and_retain_partial_reports]` has tests that pass but leave a missing or corrupt LLVM profile.
  - It asserts a failing exit status through `full_flow`.
  - It asserts the "partial profiles and reports have been retained" diagnostic.
  - It asserts there is no "Coverage check" output.
  - It asserts that each attempt succeeded, so the failure came from collection and not from test execution.
- **No exception evidence authored.** The first test seeds an `evidence` directory and asserts that `retained_files` is unchanged after both the passing run and the failing-policy run.
- **No assessment model invoked.** `model_tripwire` configures an Ollama endpoint that points at a local listener, which counts requests. The first test asserts the count is 0 after both flows.

The first test also covers the "only after the workflow succeeds" ordering from both sides. A successful workflow leads to the check running, and the failed-suite and collection-failure tests show the check is skipped.

I found no obligation without a test that asserts its outcome. The cited requirements `requirements.test-coverage.run` and `requirements.test-coverage.check` are context only, and I did not reassess their tests.
